## Repository Role and Entry Points
This is the OCA `web` repository for Odoo 18.0: a collection of independently installable addons that extend the Odoo web client, backend models, views, and selected HTTP endpoints. There is no single application entry point; Odoo discovers each addon through its manifest and package initializer, e.g. `web_responsive/__manifest__.py`, `web_timeline/__manifest__.py`, and `web_pwa_customize/__init__.py`.

## Addon Loading and Extension Boundary
Each addon is an isolated deployment unit with its own manifest, Python package, browser assets, XML views, translations, and sometimes access rules. Odoo’s module loader is the primary composition boundary; installed addons patch or register behavior into standard Odoo services, models, fields, and view types. Examples: `web_dark_mode/__manifest__.py`, `web_form_banner/__manifest__.py`, `web_widget_x2many_2d_matrix/__manifest__.py`.

## Browser Client Customizations
Most modules execute in the Odoo browser client as ES modules, patching existing controllers/renderers/models or registering UI components and field widgets. The primary flow is Odoo web-client state/action → addon JS patch/component → rendered XML/SCSS UI → ORM/RPC through Odoo’s existing client services. Representative high-impact implementations:
- Responsive shell, menus, chatter, search, and form behavior: `web_responsive/static/src/components/`, `web_responsive/static/src/views/form/form_renderer.esm.js`.
- Timeline custom view lifecycle: `web_timeline/static/src/views/timeline/timeline_view.esm.js`, `web_timeline/static/src/views/timeline/timeline_model.esm.js`.
- Pivot computed-measure UI/model extensions: `web_pivot_computed_measure/static/src/pivot/pivot_controller.esm.js`, `web_pivot_computed_measure/static/src/pivot/pivot_model.esm.js`.
- Search/filter controls: `web_filter_header_button/static/src/search/search_model_patch.esm.js`, `web_time_range_menu_custom/static/src/js/search_model.esm.js`.

## Server-Side Persistence, Configuration, and Security
Python models extend Odoo ORM entities to persist per-user/company settings, define functional records, or alter server-side behavior. XML views expose those values in Odoo administration; access CSV/XML constrains custom model access. Key examples:
- User/company presentation settings: `web_chatter_position/models/res_users.py`, `web_company_color/models/res_company.py`, `web_theme_classic/models/res_users_settings.py`.
- Configurable business/UI rules: `web_form_banner/models/web_form_banner_rule.py`, `web_quick_start_screen/models/quick_start_screen.py`.
- Security-sensitive export restriction: `web_disable_export_group/models/models.py`, `web_disable_export_group/security/groups.xml`.
- Model/view metadata manipulation for field options: `web_m2x_options_manager/models/ir_ui_view.py`, `web_m2x_options_manager/models/m2x_create_edit_option.py`.

## HTTP, Actions, and Session Boundaries
A smaller server-side layer intercepts HTTP requests, exposes endpoints, or extends Odoo action execution. These are integration boundaries between browser requests, authentication/session state, Odoo actions, and response generation:
- Dynamic Excel export behavior: `web_excel_export_dynamic_expand/controllers/excel_export.py`.
- PWA manifest endpoint and configuration: `web_pwa_customize/controllers/webmanifest.py`, `web_pwa_customize/models/res_config_settings.py`.
- Inactivity-driven logout flow: `web_session_auto_close/controllers/main.py`, `web_session_auto_close/static/src/js/session_auto_close.esm.js`.
- Multi-action and action-window messaging extensions: `web_ir_actions_act_multi/models/ir_actions.py`, `web_ir_actions_act_window_message/models/ir_actions.py`.

## Visual Assets and Third-Party Client Libraries
SCSS and XML templates are bundled into Odoo assets alongside JS, making them runtime client dependencies rather than a separately deployed frontend. The repository vendors visualization/search libraries where needed: `web_timeline/static/lib/vis-timeline/vis-timeline-graph2d.js`, `web_widget_mpld3_chart/static/src/lib/d3/d3.v5.js`, `web_responsive/static/src/lib/fuse/fuse.basic.js`. The material runtime stack is Python/Odoo on the server and JavaScript, XML templates, and SCSS in the browser; data storage and RPC are provided by the hosting Odoo instance.
